proposals.evidence: CDIAL 13982 hariṇa, meaning section 2, expressly gives Bengali harin deer. The surveyed horin forms fit that animal word. No separate stored section-2 node exists, so the containing entry is cited precisely. Exact survey form horin is preserved; uncertain intra-Indo-Aryan transmission remains open.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 10452 yāti explicitly gives Hindi jānā, Maithili jāeb and Old Marwari jāvaï go; ordinary imperative jā-/jo forms fit this verb. The article separately derives suppletive g- past forms from gata, which are not included here. Exact survey form jana is preserved; uncertain intra-Indo-Aryan transmission remains open.
